The ruined city asks to be seen

For eleven verses a speaker describes Jerusalem as “she.” In verse 12 the city begins to speak as “I.” She calls to strangers on the road, since no one else will listen. The poem says five times that she has no comforter. What she asks first is to be seen. Verse 18 admits that the LORD is right and she rebelled. That admission does not end her cry for help.
Prayer rises from the hungry streets

Verses 11–12 describe infants asking their mothers for food and dying. That picture drives the whole poem. Verse 5 says the Lord became “like an enemy.” He is still the only one to turn to. In verse 19 the poet urges Zion to pour out her heart for her children. The prayer she then offers is not gentle. Verse 20 says, “Look, LORD, and see to whom you have done thus.”
Hope interrupts grief without ending it

Verse 21 stands near the middle of the book. “This” points ahead to verses 22–23. The speaker’s situation has not changed. His hope comes from what he chooses to remember. Verse 33 adds that God does not afflict people willingly. From verse 42 the complaint returns: “you have not pardoned.” Hope interrupts the grief in this poem and does not end it.
Failed protection and the cost of hunger

The poem names three protections that failed. Prophets and priests, a foreign ally, and the king all failed (verses 13, 17, 20). It begins with the religious leaders. They should have warned the city, and they shed the blood of the just. The starving children of verses 4 and 10 are the cost. Verse 6 says a slow death by hunger is worse than Sodom’s sudden end. Verse 22 sets a limit: Zion’s punishment is complete.
A shared prayer ends without an answer

This last poem is a prayer from start to finish. The people say “we” and “us” in every part. Verse 19 says the LORD’s throne stands, though verse 18 shows his hill in ruins. Verse 21 asks God to do the turning. The people do not think they can return on their own. Verse 22 then raises the fear that he has rejected them. The book ends there, with no answer recorded.
